text: Claimed stroke-thickness + press-and-hold cards. Reading braindump.js drawing pipeline before touching anything.

Both cards reproduced in Chromium. Live stroke is pinned at 4 canvas units by CSS/braindump.css:256, which beats the stroke-width attribute: brush 24 renders 4.00 screen px live vs 24.00 baked at zoom 1, 2.00 vs 12.00 at zoom 0.5. Press-and-hold: the size bubble reads the ACTIVE tool, so pressing the eraser with the pen selected resizes the eraser 24->44 while the bubble sits frozen at 4px; and taking the pointer lock swallows the click, so the gesture never selects the tool it was performed on (measured: 0 click events with the lock, 1 without).

Done. 4 hunks in .tmp/scratch/opus5-31/patch.json (1 CSS line deleted, 3 small JS edits), nothing applied to the repo, all anchors verified unique. New suite tests/board/stroke-thickness-and-resize.test.mjs, port 4321: red on the repo (live 4.00px vs finished 24.00px), green on a patched mirror, and red again with each hunk withheld in turn. pen-and-eraser-tools, drawing-smoothness, alt-key-menu-suppression and alt-drag-copy-undo all exit 0 against the patched mirror. The tuning pipeline was NOT the cause: the baked path is the live path's own d string plus the two vertices flushStrokeTail lands at pointer-up.
